To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) family hostility (i.e., marital hostility and child-to-parent hostility) is related to depressive symptoms for middle-aged husbands and wives; (b) marital integration moderates the impact of family hostility such that for couples with low marital integration family hostility is more strongly linked with depressive symptoms; and (c) marital integration does not moderate the impact of family on depressive symptoms for those couples with high marital integration.
family hostility (i.e., chronic husband–wife marital hostility, and child hostility) is associated with depressive symptoms for both middle-aged husbands and wives.

family hostility (marital hostility and child hostility), as measured by latent constructs that reflect chronic hostile interactions, was associated with depressive symptoms in husbands’ and wives 11 years later.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of chronic family hostility and marital integration on depressive symptoms of middle-aged husbands and wives.
the impact of family hostility, specifically marital and child hostility, on depressive symptoms in husbands’ and wives.
the impact of chronic family hostility on middle-aged husbands’ (N = 370) and wives’ (N =370) depressive symptoms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of chronic marital hostility and chronic child hostility on husbands’ and wives' depressive symptoms were moderated by the level of marital integration.
the effects of family hostility on the depressive symptoms of middle-aged adults were moderated by marital integration.
family hostility has a negative effect on the depressive symptoms of both spouses, but this effect is diminished in couples who experience high levels of marital integration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the impact of marital hostility and child-hostility on the mental health of middle-aged couples is moderated by the extent to which they share activities together.
the influence of marital and family hostility on depressive symptomatology in middle-aged couples is moderated by the level of marital integration.
marital integration may serve to buffer the impact of chronic family hostility on the depressive symptoms of middle-aged husbands and wives.
The main takeaway from our work is that
marital integration may protect middle-aged adults from the adverse effects of family hostility.
marital integration is an important protective factor for middle-aged couples.

the impact of family hostility is moderated by the level of marital integration, such that couples with higher levels of marital integration experience less of an impact of family hostility than those who have low marital integration.
